manuscripts.title: A Conditional Reduction for Algebraic Kuga–Satake Correspondences
manuscripts.author: OpenAI

contexts_and_definitions.statement: Varieties are complex; cohomology is rational Betti cohomology. (S,h) is a primitively amply polarized K3 surface, h²=2d. V=h-perpendicular in H²(S,Q) has dimension 21 and signature (2,19) for the cup form q. T=NS(S)_Q-perpendicular is contained in V, contains the period plane, and has dimension at least two. Q(1) shifts Hodge types by (-1,-1); the Hodge circle acts on type (p,q) by exp(i(p-q)θ).

Fix a rational quadratic polarization Q on T, the full even Clifford construction, an invertible odd right multiplier identifying parity spaces, a rational weight-one polarization, and a specified isogenous abelian realization A_S with W_S=H¹(A_S,Q). These data determine κ_S:T→W_S⊗W_S→H²(A_S×A_S,Q) in the ordered mixed Künneth summand. Exact realization means Γ_S∈CH²(S×A_S×A_S)_Q with (p_AA)_*(cl(Γ_S)∪p_S*x)=κ_S(x) for every x∈T, with every normalization retained.

H is rational of weight two and K3 type, with h²⁰=h⁰²=1 and only types (2,0),(1,1),(0,2). Q is nondegenerate, of sign ε=±1 on the oriented period plane and the opposite sign on its orthogonal complement. The relation is v²=Q(v,v). For H²⁰=C(e₁+i e₂), Q(e_j,e_j)=ε and e₁⊥e₂, J=εe₁e₂ and g_θ=cos θ+J sin θ act by left multiplication on the full parity spaces P_H^±=C^±(H,Q), with the i-eigenspace of L_J designated (1,0).

A chosen weight-one polarization gives j_P:P∨(-1)≅P. For f:H(1)→Hom(P,M), its tensor form is H→M⊗P∨(-1)→M⊗P. When H⊂H²(S,Q), algebraic realization means exactly this restricted action of a codimension-two rational cycle on S×A_M×A_P, with algebraic target projectors available to remove other Künneth components.

The recovery section assumes Hg(V)=SO(V,q) for the rank-21 primitive K3 space, not a genericity condition on the witness abelian variety. In the joint group of V, U=H¹(B,Q), and W^±=C^±(V,q), the distinguished rational Lie ideal is g≅so(V,q). Its complex spin module Δ has dimension 2¹⁰.

On a connected complex manifold, 'very general' means outside a countable union of proper closed analytic subsets. Specialization concerns actual rational cycle classes, not merely flat classes that are Hodge, and retains the entire prescribed class and its coefficients.

For smooth projective P,Q, Z∈CH^a(P×Q)_Q acts H^j(P)→H^{j+2e}(Q)(e), e=a-dim P, by pullback, cup with cl(Z), and pushforward. Composition subtracts the dimension of the intermediate variety from the sum of codimensions.

claims.label: main:generic
claims.statement: Assume Hg(V)=SO(V,q). The following are equivalent: (i) some complex abelian B and α∈CH²(S×B)_Q induce a nonzero map α_*:V→H²(B,Q); (ii) some smooth connected projective surface Y admits a dominant generically finite morphism f:Y→S for which the trace f_* of the image of Λ²H⁰(Y,Ω¹_Y)→H⁰(Y,Ω²_Y) is nonzero; (iii) for any stipulated standard data on T, a cycle Γ_S exactly realizes κ_S as in eq:cycle-target. In this situation T=V. The same input realizes the standard full primitive Clifford construction with the cup form.

claims.label: main:specialization
claims.statement: Fix a component of the moduli space of primitively amply polarized K3 surfaces of degree 2d. If condition (i) or (ii) of main:generic holds very generally in that component, then every (S,h) in it has the exact prescribed cycle Γ_S for every stipulated standard datum on T(S). It suffices that, about each desired point, the input holds outside countably many proper closed analytic subsets of a full polarized period chart; an algebraically very-general input suffices. Witness cycles, abelian varieties, and covers need not vary in a family.

claims.label: main:all-degrees
claims.statement: If the hypothesis of main:specialization holds in the required polarized components in every degree, then every projective K3 surface has a cycle realizing its prescribed κ_S.

claims.label: cyc:h1
claims.statement: For complex abelian varieties P,Q, pullback identifies Hom(Q,P)⊗Q with Hom_HS(H¹(P,Q),H¹(Q,Q)). Arbitrary rational weight-one Hodge maps therefore act algebraically and independently on the two slots of an ordered tensor product of first cohomologies; they need not preserve chosen polarizations.

claims.label: cyc:projectors
claims.statement: Every cohomological Künneth projector on a product of abelian varieties is induced by a rational algebraic correspondence. For U=H¹(B,Q), the mixed part of pullback along addition B×B→B injects H²(B,Q)=Λ²U into U⊗U by u∧v↦u⊗v−v⊗u.

claims.label: cyc:descent
claims.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional rational vector space of cohomological maps and E_alg its subspace of actions of rational algebraic correspondences of a fixed degree. For every field extension K/Q, E∩(E_alg⊗K)=E_alg inside E⊗K. The assertion remains true after restricting actions to a specified rational source subspace.

claims.label: cyc:equivalence
claims.statement: Under the full-Hodge-group setting of main:generic, its nonzero correspondence condition (i) and surface-cover wedge-trace condition (ii) are equivalent. The implication from (ii) to a nonzero correspondence on V does not require the full Hodge-group hypothesis; the converse uses injectivity on V.

claims.label: cliff:construction
claims.statement: For H,Q and the sign/orientation conventions of context:clifford, P_H^± are polarizable weight-one Hodge structures; m^Q:H(1)→Hom(P_H^+,P_H^-), x↦L_x, is a rational Hodge embedding. Right multiplication by any fixed invertible odd Clifford element gives a rational Hodge isomorphism of the parity spaces. On a sufficiently small period chart their filtrations vary holomorphically and admit fixed rational polarizations.

claims.label: cliff:slots
claims.statement: If f:H(1)→Hom(P,M) is algebraically realized and a:M→M', b:P'→P are rational weight-one Hodge maps, then x↦a f(x)b is algebraically realized. This remains true under changing chosen duality isomorphisms, interchanging tensor factors with the appropriate Künneth sign, and rational Hodge identifications with isogenous abelian models.

claims.label: gen:genericity
claims.statement: In every sufficiently small full-dimensional marked polarized period chart, Hg(V)=SO(V,q) holds outside a countable union of proper closed analytic subsets. At every such point V is irreducible as a rational Hodge structure and T(S)=V.

claims.label: gen:joint-group
claims.statement: Assume Hg(V)=SO(V,q), let B be any complex abelian variety, U=H¹(B,Q), W^±=C^±(V,q), and let h be the Lie algebra of their joint Hodge group with V. Then h=g⊕k as commuting rational ideals, g≅so(V,q), and k is the kernel on V. The ideal k acts trivially on both W^±, and g acts there by the usual left spin action.

claims.label: gen:width
claims.statement: In the joint-group setting, U_C=(Δ⊗M)⊕M₀ and W_C^±=Δ⊗N_± as g_C-modules, where M₀ is trivial and dim N_±=2¹⁰. Every rational g-equivariant map U→W^± is a weight-one Hodge map, and Hom_HS(U,W^±)⊗C=Hom_g_C(U_C,W_C^±)≅Hom_C(M,N_±).

claims.label: gen:vector-multiplicity
claims.statement: For the vector module V_C of so₂₁(C) and its spin module Δ, Hom_g_C(V_C,Δ⊗Δ) has dimension one. Neither Δ nor the trivial representation contains a copy of V_C.

claims.label: gen:generation
claims.statement: Assume Hg(V)=SO(V,q), and suppose some α∈CH²(S×B)_Q induces a nonzero V→H²(B,Q). For every ε₁,ε₂∈{+,-}, every abelian realization H¹(A_j,Q)=W^{ε_j}, and every rational Hodge map β:V→W^{ε₁}⊗W^{ε₂}⊂H²(A₁×A₂,Q), there exists Γ∈CH²(S×A₁×A₂)_Q whose action restricted to V is β. In particular the full primitive Clifford multiplication tensor and its prescribed even-Clifford realization are recovered.

claims.label: spec:hilbert-map
claims.statement: Let p:X→D be a smooth proper holomorphic family of nonempty pure n-dimensional varieties over a connected complex manifold, equipped with a relative embedding X⊂D×P^N. Then there are a reduced complex quasi-projective scheme H, a smooth projective algebraic family U→H, and a holomorphic η:D→H^an such that X is its embedded analytic pullback.

claims.label: spec:flat-cycle
claims.statement: Let f:M→R be a smooth projective algebraic family of relative dimension n over a smooth irreducible complex variety R of dimension b. If Z⊂M is flat over R with fibers of dimension n−2, then r↦cl([Z_r]_{n−2}) in H⁴(M_r,Q) is a section of R⁴f_*^an Q. The notation [Z_r]_{n−2} uses generic scheme lengths and ignores smaller-dimensional components; the claim includes nonpure and nonreduced fibers.

claims.label: spec:specialization
claims.statement: Let D be a connected polydisc and p:X→D a smooth proper holomorphic family of n-dimensional varieties, n≥2, with a relative embedding in D×P^N. For a flat rational θ∈H⁰(D,R⁴p_*Q), if θ_t is the class of a rational codimension-two algebraic cycle for very general t, then it is such a class for every t∈D.

claims.label: spec:local
claims.statement: For any primitively amply polarized (S₀,h), after shrinking a full-dimensional polarized period polydisc D about its period, there exist smooth proper holomorphic K3 and abelian families S→D and A→D. The K3 family has central fiber (S₀,h), relative ample line bundle and integral H² marking; its primitive rational local system is the fixed rank-21 (V,q). The abelian family's marked H¹ is the full W=C⁺(V,q). Fixed rational polarization and parity data give flat standard tensors μ_t:V→H¹(A_t)⊗H¹(A_t). After shrinking, S×_D A×_D A embeds relatively in D×P^N.

claims.label: spec:primitive
claims.statement: Fix a polarized moduli component. If the nonzero algebraic input of main:generic holds very generally, then at every (S₀,h) in that component the standard full primitive Clifford tensor is induced by a rational codimension-two cycle. The same holds for an input outside countably many proper closed analytic subsets of a full polarized chart about each desired point.

claims.label: data:restriction

contexts_and_definitions.statement: Coefficients are rational. HC is surjectivity CH^r(X)_Q→H^{2r}(X,Q)∩H^{r,r}(X) for smooth projective complex X. N^pH^j(X,Q) is the sum, over closed B⊂X of codimension at least p, of kernels of restriction to X\B; GHC identifies this with the largest rational sub-Hodge structure with both Hodge indices at least p. Later N^p=H^j for p≤0. For a projective K3 S, T_S=NS(S)_Q-perpendicular in H²(S,Q) with its actual cup form q has signature (2,20−ρ(S)).

For a K3-type quadratic space (T,q), use v²=q(v,v), the full W=C⁺(T,q), and the left complex structure L_J for J=e₁e₂ when T²⁰=C(e₁+i e₂) with an oriented positive orthonormal pair. Fix H¹(A,Q)=W, a rational nonisotropic w∈T, and rational polarization E. The exact map is j_w:T(1)→End(W), j_w(v)(a)=vaw. In End(W)=W⊗W∨, apply (E^flat)^−1 to the dual slot after untwisting to obtain ι_{w,E}:T→W⊗W⊂H²(A²,Q). The choice of w need not be a Hodge vector. 'Standard' means this specified map, not an arbitrary embedding.

The hyperbolic plane U has Gram matrix [[0,1],[1,0]]. P=U⊕D₈(−1)⊕D₄(−1); T_P=U⊕U(2)⊕D₄(−1); V_P=(T_P)_Q≅U_Q²⊥⟨−1⟩⁴ has dimension eight and signature (2,6). An ample P-polarization is a primitive embedding P→NS(S) whose image contains an ample class. U_P=P_Q-perpendicular retains rank eight at Picard jumps, when it may strictly contain T_S.

Cohomology is rational Betti unless an integral lattice is specified; integral cohomology is modulo torsion. A cycle Z∈CH^r(M×N)_Q acts H^k(M)→H^{k+2r−2dim M}(N) by pullback, product and pushforward, with the corresponding Tate twist. Projectors mean algebraic correspondences acting idempotently on cohomology, not necessarily idempotence in Chow.

For S, set N=NS(S)_Q, T=N-perpendicular, V=T(1). A point o, a divisor basis D_i and its inverse intersection matrix b^{ij} give π₀=[o]×S, π₄=S×[o], π_N=Σb^{ij}D_i×D_j and π_T=Δ−π₀−π₄−π_N. Products of π_T and Alt_k=(1/k!)Σsgn(σ)σ cut out Λ^kT⊂H^{2k}(S^k,Q), self-adjointly with nondegenerate exterior pairing. Algebraic coefficient extension means scalar extension of the rational cycle-class image, with rational descent H_Q∩(A_Q⊗K)=A_Q.

B is an indecomposable principally polarized abelian surface, M=O_B(H) a symmetric principal theta bundle, and χ∈Pic⁰(B)[4] has exact order four. A normalized section d∈H⁰(B,M²) cuts out a smooth D avoiding B[2]. Work on algebraic affine section charts ℓ(d)=1 of the six-dimensional parameter space. π:B'→B is the degree-two isogeny for χ², with π_*O=O⊕χ²; choose a trivialization of π*χ². Let L=π*(Mχ) and X→B' be z²=π*d. δ is the sheet involution and j the commuting lift of inversion from the normalized symmetric linearization of L. U_X=H²(X,Q)^{j=1,δ=−1}.

On the good open of geom:gauss-generic, the regular Gauss fibers on D are {±x₁,…,±x₄}. Over their regular-value open R⊂P¹, the 16 selections contain one point from each opposite pair. s[p] flips the chosen signed point p. The two parity covers and their smooth projective completions C_± need not be connected; they share a coherent half-sum assignment.

V here denotes the integral anti-invariant lattice of Y of signature (2,14), not T(1) from the earlier criterion section; U is its rational rank-eight summand with the Y-pairing. The lattice enlargement called M in the pencil section is unrelated to the theta bundle M. A section pencil is d_t=d₀+t d₁ on the original affine t-line, ℓ(d₀)=1, ℓ(d₁)=0, with leading section smooth and avoiding two-torsion.

A polarized ADE K3 is a normal surface with rational double points whose minimal resolution is a K3, with a primitive ample relative Picard class. A smooth quasi-polarization is primitive big and nef. Fix a positive primitive h in Λ_K3; D_h is a component of the isotropic positive-line domain in h-perpendicular; Γ_h fixes h and preserves that component. P_h=[Γ_h\D_h] is the integral period stack. Contractions are canonical polarized contractions; scalar automorphisms of representing line bundles are removed by the relative-Picard convention.

For one fixed original pencil O⊂A¹_t, compare a smooth projective K3 family S→O and a smooth projective connected-surface family X→O. The first substitution t=s+u² gives threefolds, fixed compactifications and a degree-three correspondence before b is chosen. The second s=b+v² gives the conic u²+v²=(t−b)w²; its two complete components at t=b give difference cylinders. φ between the degree-two subvariations need not be an isometry; in the geometric application φ* q_X=2q_Y.

For U of dimension eight and signature (2,6), W=C⁺(U,q) has rational dimension 128. Over C its left action consists of eight copies of each eight-dimensional half-spin S_±. Recovery uses both ordered tensor orientations and ordinary tensor flip; on the mixed H¹⊗H¹ summand the geometric interchange acts as minus that ordinary flip.

claims.label: ext:criterion
claims.statement: Let S be any projective K3 surface. Suppose that for one rational nonisotropic w∈T_S, one rational weight-one polarization and one full even-Clifford realization H¹(A,Q)=C⁺(T_S,q), the tensor of j_w(v)(a)=vaw is induced by a cycle in CH²(S×A²)_Q. Then rational HC and rational GHC hold in every degree of every self-power S^m.

claims.label: main:theorem
claims.statement: Let S be a smooth projective complex K3 surface with a rational isometric embedding of its actual transcendental cup-product space (T_S,q) into V_P. For every full realization H¹(A,Q)=C⁺(T_S,q), every rational nonisotropic w∈T_S and every rational polarization E of that weight-one structure, a cycle Γ_S∈CH²(S×A×A)_Q acts on every x∈T_S as exactly ι_{w,E}(x) in full H²(A²,Q). The same holds for any specified transported isogenous model. Moreover rational HC and GHC hold in every degree of S^m for every m≥1. All ample P-polarized surfaces, including Picard jumps, satisfy the embedding hypothesis.

claims.label: main:lattice
claims.statement: P admits a primitive embedding in Λ_K3=U³⊕E₈(−1)² whose integral orthogonal complement is T_P=U⊕U(2)⊕D₄(−1). For every primitive embedding P→Λ_K3, the rational orthogonal complement is isometric to V_P.

claims.label: ext:conditional
claims.statement: Let S be projective K3, t=dim_Q T, V=T(1), and W=C⁺(T,q)=H¹(A,Q). Suppose one exact j_w tensor, for rational nonisotropic w and a rational polarization, is induced by CH²(S×A²)_Q. For every 1≤k≤t there is an injective algebraic Hodge map F_k:Λ^kV→End(W) with algebraic left inverse on cohomology. For Z=A² and n=dim Z, it is realized by Γ_k∈CH^{k+1}(S^k×Z)_Q and R_k∈CH^{n+k−1}(Z×S^k)_Q, with R_k*F_k=id using End(W)≅(H¹(A)⊗H¹(A))(1)⊂H²(Z)(1) and Λ^kV⊂H^{2k}(S^k)(k). Every rational Hodge class in Λ^kV is a codimension-k rational algebraic cycle class on S^k.

claims.label: ghc:lem:cycle-support
claims.statement: For smooth projective X,Y of dimensions N,D and any C∈CH^{N+p}(X×Y)_Q with p≥0, there is a fixed closed B⊂Y of codimension at least p supporting the entire cohomological image of C. In particular C_*H^j(X,Q)⊂N^pH^{j+2p}(Y,Q) for every j.

claims.label: ghc:prop:exterior-coniveau
claims.statement: If S satisfies ext:conditional's exact even-Clifford algebraicity premise, then for every 1≤k≤t=dim_Q T, Λ^kT⊂N^{k−1}H^{2k}(S^k,Q). Every rational sub-Hodge structure of this exterior power satisfies GHC in that ambient cohomology. In particular the top exterior line Λ^tT is supported in codimension t.

claims.label: ghc:lem:orthogonal-carriers
claims.statement: Let V=T(1) for a projective K3 with Hg(V)=SO(V,q), t=dim V≥3. Let H be a nontrivial rational simple representation occurring in a direct sum of tensor powers of V, with its induced weight-zero Hodge structure of Hodge level at most 2b. Then there are c,s≥1 and integers 1≤k_i≤t with c≤b and s=Σk_i, and a surjective rational Hodge map ⊗_{i=1}^c Λ^{k_i}V→H.

claims.label: ghc:lem:k3-carriers
claims.statement: For V=T(1) of any projective K3 and G=Hg(V), let H be a nontrivial rational simple G-representation occurring in a direct sum of tensor powers of V, with induced Hodge level at most 2b. Then for some 1≤c≤b and 1≤k₁,…,k_c≤dim_Q V there is a surjective rational Hodge map ⊗_{j=1}^cΛ^{k_j}V→H. The claim includes totally real and CM endomorphism fields, rational nonsplit forms and all actual rational constituents.

claims.label: geom:structure
claims.statement: For the stated smooth abelian double-cover data there is a smooth double cover Y→K=Km(B'), K resolved, such that: (i) V=H²(Y,Z)^{δ=−1} modulo torsion is even of signature (2,14) with 2-elementary discriminant group, and fixed-(B,M,χ) monodromy is trivial on that group; (ii) eight mutually orthogonal algebraic anti-invariant classes a_i of square −4 have perpendicular U⊂V_Q of signature (2,6), rationally isometric to V_P with the Y intersection form; (iii) resolved pullback gives a flat Hodge isomorphism β:U≅U_X with (βx,βy)_X=2(x,y)_Y, and e=(Δ_X+Γ_j−Γ_δ−Γ_{jδ})/4∈CH²(X×X)_Q has image U_X in degree two and vanishes in every other degree. All constructions are compatible with the indicated smooth parameter opens.

claims.label: geom:twisted-hodge
claims.statement: Set E=T_B(−log D). U_X admits a flat complex identification with a character eigenspace having U_X^{p,q}≅H^q(B,Ω_B^p(log D)⊗M^−1χ), p+q=2; in particular U_X^{2,0}=H⁰(B,Mχ) is one-dimensional. The full six-dimensional family tangent space identifies with H¹(B,E) by Kodaira–Spencer.

claims.label: geom:period
claims.statement: The period map of U, equivalently U_X, has rank six on a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the six-dimensional parameter space. For very general parameters U is simple, has no nonzero rational (1,1) class, and has Hodge group SO(U).

claims.label: geom:gauss-generic
claims.statement: On a nonempty Zariski-open set of (B,D) parameters, D has no nontrivial translation stabilizer, C=D/{±1} is smooth of genus three, and D→C is a connected étale double cover defined by nontrivial ε∈Pic⁰(C)[2]. The Gauss map factors D→C→P¹ with degrees two and four, the latter map given by |K_C⊗ε|. No fiber of that degree-four map has all multiplicities even. The good open remains nonempty on every component after the finite theta, torsion and level choices defining X.

claims.label: geom:halves
claims.statement: There is an algebraic h:Selections→B with 2h(s)=Σ_{p∈s}p and h(s[p])=h(s)−p. The selection cover splits globally by parity into degree-eight covers S_+ and S_−. Their possibly disconnected smooth projective completions C_± carry extensions a_±:C_±→B. At every point where a_± has nonzero differential it is tangent to the direction recorded by its P¹ parameter.

claims.statement: On a regular-value disc, no signed sum of a nonempty subset of the four local branches x_i is constant. Every connected component of C_± maps nonconstantly to B. No image component Z_+ from C_+ and Z_− from C_− satisfies Z_+=b−Z_− for any b∈B.

claims.label: geom:domination
claims.statement: For every parameter in a nonempty Zariski-open subset there exist smooth projective connected curves C₁,C₂ and a dominant generically finite morphism g:C₁×C₂→X. If additionally U_X has no nonzero rational (1,1) class, an algebraic correspondence injects U_X into H¹(C₁,Q)⊗H¹(C₂,Q). Thus the injection exists at very general parameters.

claims.label: geom:genericity
claims.statement: Every nonempty regular period chart admits a smaller normalized product chart A×Q of abelian data and affine section coordinates in the simultaneous geometric open of geom:period and geom:domination. Given any countable collection of proper closed analytic period loci in the original chart, one can successively choose: abelian data a in a residual subset of A; for each such a, a section pencil in a residual subset of each prescribed nonempty admissible pencil open meeting Q; then, after fixing that pencil, all but countably many points of its intersection with Q and a nonempty algebraic good open. These points avoid the prescribed loci. Proper marked rational Hodge-tensor exceptions on the connected smooth pencil part are countable. The pencils are d_t=d₀+t d₁ with ℓ(d₀)=1, ℓ(d₁)=0 and d₁ smooth avoiding two-torsion. Further pencil-specific countable exclusions may be added after the pencil is fixed; no uniform exceptional list across pencils is claimed.

claims.label: pencil:realization
claims.statement: Choose abelian data and d_t=d₀+t d₁ in geom:genericity's generic sets. There is a nonempty algebraic O⊂A¹_t and a smooth projective K3 family S⁰→O with a flat isometric embedding U→R²(S⁰/O)_*Q, using U's cup form inherited from Y. For very general t, U_t is the entire transcendental part of H²(S⁰_t,Q). For every s in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of A¹_s, every smooth projective model of the total family pulled back by t=s+u² is uniruled. The K3 family is defined over the original t-line; no unspecified finite base change remains.

claims.statement: Let V be an even lattice of signature (2,14) with elementary 2-primary discriminant group, and G⊂O(V) act trivially on that group. Then there exist an even finite-index overlattice M of V, a primitive embedding M→Λ_K3, and a primitive positive h∈M-perpendicular such that G extends to Λ_K3 acting identically on M-perpendicular.

claims.label: pencil:monodromy
claims.statement: For the general normalized section pencil with fixed abelian data and smooth leading section avoiding two-torsion, monodromy on V at every finite singular parameter is a product of reflections in mutually orthogonal integral (−2)-roots in V, perpendicular to the limiting Hodge line. After killing those finite monodromies, the periods extend to interior periods. At infinity monodromy on V is −id.

claims.label: pencil:periodstack
claims.statement: There is a morphism q:P_h=[Γ_h\D_h]→M_h, the moduli stack of primitively polarized ADE K3 surfaces of degree (h,h), whose composite with the smooth quasi-polarized period map is canonical polarized contraction. Pullback of the Hodge line is the tautological period line with its full Γ_h-linearization. At [σ], the stabilizer-map kernel is exactly the group W_σ generated by reflections in roots r∈Λ_K3 with r²=−2, (r,h)=0 and (r,σ)=0.

claims.label: pencil:descent
claims.statement: Let C be a smooth projective complex curve, D⊂C finite, C°=C\D. Suppose (i) L is a Λ_K3 local system on C° with flat positive primitive h; (ii) a holomorphic line F⊂L⊗O has (F,F)=0, (σ,bar σ)>0 for nonzero σ∈F, and (F,h)=0; (iii) every puncture has finite local monodromy and an interior limiting period after a killing cover. Then a normal projective model Z→C restricts on C° to a polarized ADE K3 family realizing the data modulo contracted roots. If at every puncture monodromy is in the Weyl group generated by roots perpendicular to h and the limiting F, Z→C may be flat ADE everywhere, its Hodge line descends to λ on C, and ω_{Z/C}=f*λ, K_Z=f*(K_C⊗λ). Independently of this extra Weyl condition, if nondegenerate U⊂L_Q contains F and every locally flat root persistently of type (1,1) is perpendicular to U, then on a smaller nonempty algebraic open of C° there is a smooth projective K3 family S⁰ realizing U isometrically as a Hodge summand, without changing C.

claims.label: pencil:uniruledcriterion
claims.statement: Under the Weyl condition in pencil:descent, if deg(K_C⊗λ)<0, every smooth projective model of the function field of Z is uniruled.

claims.label: comp:twosquares
claims.statement: Let O⊂A¹_t be nonempty Zariski open and S→O, X→O smooth projective families of connected surfaces, with S fibers K3. Assume: (i) a polarized rational K3-type subvariation U⊂R²f_*Q has nondegenerate restricted cup form, nonconstant period, and simple fibers outside a countable set; (ii) commuting involutions j,δ on X give e=(1+j)(1−δ)/4 annihilating R^qg_*Q for q≠2, with a specified VHS isomorphism φ:U≅eR²g_*Q; (iii) for s in a nonempty Zariski open, both total families pulled back by t=s+u² have smooth projective uniruled threefold models. Then there are nonempty Zariski-open G⊂O and countable E⊂G such that every b∈G\E has Θ_b∈CH²(S_b×X_b)_Q inducing exactly φ_b on U_b. G and all auxiliaries used before choosing b can be fixed for that pencil.

claims.label: comp:models
claims.statement: For a smooth projective surface family Y→O in this section, the first square pullbacks admit models Z projective over A¹_s and nonempty open G⊂O with Z_G→G smooth. For every b∈G one can choose a smooth projective fourfold M_b mapping to P¹_t and P¹_v whose inverse images of V₀={v∈A¹:b+v²∈G} and O are respectively Z_G×_G V₀ (s=b+v²) and Y×_O Q_b, Q_b={u²+v²=(t−b)w²}⊂O×P². claims.label: comp:surface
claims.statement: Fix abelian-cover data and a section pencil satisfying geom:structure, geom:period and pencil:realization, with nonconstant U-period along it and simple U_t outside a countable set. On a nonempty open of that pencil, for all but countably many b, there exists Θ_b∈CH²(S⁰_b×X_b)_Q inducing on U_b the specified identification with H²(X_b)^{j=+,δ=−}.

claims.label: final:curves
claims.statement: Choose abelian data and a pencil as in geom:genericity, then b in the common good open outside the countable exceptions of that lemma and comp:surface. Then smooth projective curves C₁,C₂ and Z∈CH²(S⁰_b×C₁×C₂)_Q exist whose action injects U_b→H¹(C₁,Q)⊗H¹(C₂,Q). Here U_b=T_{S⁰_b} and Hg(U_b)=SO(U_b).

claims.label: final:spin
claims.statement: Let (U,q) be eight-dimensional polarized rational K3 type of signature (2,6), Hg(U)=SO(U,q), W_i polarized effective weight one, and W=C⁺(U,q) with its KS structure. For every nonzero rational Hodge f:U→W₁⊗W₂, set H=Hom_HS(W₁,W)⊗Hom_HS(W₂,W). The map Φ:H⊕H→Hom_HS(U,W⊗W), (a⊗b,0)↦(a⊗b)f and (0,a⊗b)↦τ(a⊗b)f with ordinary flip τ, is surjective. If U⊂H²(M,Q) for a smooth projective surface, W_i=H¹(C_i,Q), W=H¹(A,Q), and f is induced by a codimension-two cycle M→C₁×C₂, every target map is induced by CH²(M×A×A)_Q.

If that successful set contains a nonempty open, or escapes every countable union of proper closed analytic subsets, it equals B.

In the totally real case a nondegenerate symmetric E-form φ has trace q and Hg(T(1))=Res_{E/Q}SO(T,φ); in the CM case φ is Hermitian over E/E⁺ and Hg(T(1))=Res_{E⁺/Q}U(T,φ), the full unitary group. manuscripts.title: Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties
manuscripts.author: OpenAI

contexts_and_definitions.statement: Fix Qbar⊂C, a prime p and a p-adic place w of Qbar. F=algebraic closure of F_p, K₀=Frac W(F), and C_w is the completion of Qbar at w. K₀ and an algebraic closure of it are regarded as subfields of C_w. Good reduction means after descent to a number field and finite extension at the chosen place. The prime and place stay fixed; no comparison between different places is asserted.

For X/F, H_v^{2r}(X)(r) denotes ℓ-adic cohomology over k_ℓ=Q_ℓ for ℓ≠p, and crystalline cohomology extended from K₀ to k_p=C_w for v=p. Traces use the top Tate twist and send zero-cycle classes to degrees. Hodge-class specializations are absolute-Hodge/smooth-proper away from p and de Rham–crystalline at p. Tensor operations, divisor classes and homomorphisms use the same comparison normalizations. First crystalline cohomology remains over K₀ when filtrations are constructed.

Work up to isogeny: Hom⁰(X,Y)=Hom(X,Y)⊗Q. For a rational homomorphism f, pullback on H¹ extends to the exterior algebra; if Nf is integral, f*=N^(−2r)(Nf)* on H^{2r}, simultaneously in every realization. Rational divisor coefficients and denominators divisible by p are allowed after inverting p.

Lef^r(X) is rational divisor-polynomial expressions of codimension r modulo numerical equivalence. A simultaneous rational Lefschetz class is the tuple of realizations of one fixed element of this Q-space, not merely a tuple lying separately in its local scalar spans. The manuscript imports injective realization, perfect complementary pairing, stability under homomorphism pushforward, and hard Lefschetz plus its inverse on these subspaces.

contexts_and_definitions.label: build/sections/01_preliminaries.tex:L108-L113
contexts_and_definitions.statement: A tuple α=(α_v)_v with α_v∈H_v^{2r}(X)(r) has the Lefschetz pairing property if for every δ∈Lef^{dim X−r}(X), all Tr_v(α_vδ_v) are images of one rational number. The rational number may depend on δ and α.

Finite local-field descent means the isocrystal and indicated tensors descend to H₀, the maximal unramified subfield of a finite H/Q_p, with filtration over H; extension is to K₀H. A tensor-preserving identification respects a finite rational tensor family whose stabilizer is the chosen group, together with all comparison realizations.

A full Bruhat–Tits stabilizer is the smooth group scheme fixing a point of the extended building; its identity component is parahoric. The cited strongly admissible triple (H,X_H,H_model) is Hodge type, has full stabilizer with connected special fiber, R-smooth centralizer of a maximal K₀-split torus, and reduced relative root system over K₀ when p=2. The source invokes R-smoothness only for products/extensions of induced split tori.

For x in the integral Hodge-type model, C_x is its abelian variety, D_x=H¹_cris(C_x/W(F))[1/p], and s_{α,0,x}, s_{α,ℓ,x} are canonical specialized tensors. I_x consists of y admitting one actual abelian quasi-isogeny C_x→C_y preserving the crystalline tensors and every prime-to-p tensor. Separate unrelated local linear maps do not define membership.

For an isocrystal D/K₀ and finite K/K₀, a subspace L⊂D_K defines Fil^i=D_K for i≤0, Fil¹=L, Fil^i=0 for i≥2. For every subisocrystal P⊂D over the fixed K₀, t_H(P)=dim_K(P_K∩L), t_N(P) is its slope sum, v(p)=1. Weak admissibility requires t_H(D)=t_N(D) and t_H(P)≤t_N(P) for every such P. Finite local-field descent is separate, not inferred merely from weak admissibility over K₀.

A/Qbar has good reduction at w, a rational action of a CM field E with conjugation e↦bar e, and polarization λ whose Rosati restricts to conjugation. For V=H₁(A(C),Q), dim_E V=2s, s≥1, dim A=g=s[E:Q], and every E-embedding has Hodge multiplicities (s,s). The alternating polarization ψ satisfies ψ(ex,y)=ψ(x,bar e y). Balanced signatures are not the stronger split-Weil-type condition that a related Hermitian form have a half-dimensional isotropic subspace.

contexts_and_definitions.label: def:weil-space
contexts_and_definitions.statement: W_E^s(A)⊂Λ_Q^{2s}V∨⊗Q(s)=H^{2s}(A(C),Q(s)) is the rational subspace whose extension to a splitting field Ω of E is the direct sum over τ:E→Ω of Λ_Ω^{2s}V_τ∨⊗Q(s)_Ω, each determinant form extended by zero on the other eigenspaces. The sum is Galois stable. Balanced signatures make these rational classes Hodge classes.

For the reduced polarization, U={u∈End⁰(A₀):u†=u and ue=bar e u for every e∈E}. The dichotomy tests invertibility in the rational endomorphism algebra. An invertible such u gives a divisor form D^u(x,y)=ψ₀(x,uy), nondegenerate separately on each same-embedding E-eigenspace.

On homology V, let c be the GSp multiplier and define G={a∈GSp(V,ψ)∩GL_E(V):det_E(a)=c(a)^s}, the equality taken in E⊗R with scalar right-hand side for every Q-algebra R. Its dual cohomological form uses inverse multiplier under contragredient group action; the pullback action of an individual endomorphism is separately distinguished in the filtration proof.

S₀ is the class of F-varieties whose connected components are products of abelian varieties and projective spaces. After applying Milne2009 Theorem 4.5 to CM rationality, fix one good theory R of rational Tate classes before varying A or γ. Its rational spaces are stable under pullback, inject into realizations, and contain CM Hodge specializations. Its native crystalline components are over K₀; equality to γ_{0,p} is after extension to C_w. This membership statement by itself asserts no algebraic cycle.

The figure distinguishes CM transport A^n→C only on reductions a_CM:A₀^n→C₀, with γ₀=(a_CM j)*κ₀, from prescribed-filtration transport of a separately chosen balanced Weil variety Z, a_fl:Z₀^m→B₀, with a_fl*Fil¹H¹_dR(B)=(F_Z¹)^⊕m. Vertical arrows are good reduction. The caption explicitly claims no map between generic fibers; B may be local and need not be CM, and the auxiliaries need not coincide.

claims.label: thm:main
claims.statement: Let A/Qbar have dimension d and good reduction A₀/F at w, let 0≤r≤d, and let γ∈H^{2r}(A(C),Q(r)) be rational Hodge. For every list of Cartier divisors D₁,…,D_{d−r} on A₀ there is q∈Q such that Tr_ℓ(γ_{0,ℓ}∏c₁,ℓ(D_i))=q in Q_ℓ for every ℓ≠p and Tr_p(γ_{0,p}∏c₁,cris(D_i))=q in C_w. Here γ_{0,p}∈H^{2r}_cris(A₀/W(F))[1/p](r)⊗_{K₀}C_w and traces send zero-cycle classes to degrees. For r=d the product is 1. This covers all p including 2, divisors that do not lift, and by linearity complementary rational Lefschetz classes.

claims.label: lem:comparison
claims.statement: For an abelian variety with good reduction, realizations of an absolute Hodge class are compatible with de Rham and crystalline comparisons; the tensor obtained from its p-adic étale realization equals, after scalar extension, its de Rham–crystalline realization in thm:main. This respects tensor operations, duals, Tate twists, divisors and rational homomorphisms. The same applies to good-reduction auxiliaries over a finite extension of K₀, using an abstract complex embedding of an algebraic closure of their definition field.

claims.label: lem:pairing-functorial
claims.statement: If a tuple α has the Lefschetz pairing property on an abelian variety Y/F and f∈Hom⁰(X,Y), then f*α has it on X. The claim allows arbitrary rational homomorphisms, not just isogenies; degree-out-of-range cases give zero.

claims.label: lem:lift-hom
claims.statement: Let R be a complete mixed-characteristic DVR finite over W(F), K its fraction field, X,Y abelian schemes over R and f₀∈Hom⁰(X₀,Y₀). If the contravariant crystalline map of this specified rational algebraic f₀ preserves the Hodge filtrations, f₀ lifts uniquely to a rational homomorphism X→Y. A symmetric such X₀→X₀∨ lifts to a rational divisor class on the generic fiber (after finite extension if needed in the proof). Algebraic identities among finitely many lifted maps remain valid. No arbitrary Q_p-linear cohomology map is asserted algebraic.

claims.label: prop:transport
claims.statement: Let A/Qbar have positive dimension and good reduction, V=H₁(A(C),Q), and G⊂GSp(V,ψ) be connected reductive with Hodge homomorphism h of A and a conjugacy class X making this a Hodge embedding. Suppose γ is rational Hodge of codimension r whose alternating form satisfies γ(gv₁,…,gv_{2r})=c(g)^rγ(v₁,…,v_{2r}) for G's multiplier c. Then there are n>0, a good-reduction B, one quasi-isogeny a:A₀^n→B₀ and rational Hodge κ of codimension r with (aj)*κ₀=γ₀, simultaneously for every ℓ≠p and crystalline cohomology extended to C_w, j the first-factor inclusion. One may require either (1) B CM over Qbar at w; or (2) given a degree-(0,1) weakly admissible filtration F_A on D_A=H¹_cris(A₀)[1/p] over finite K/K₀, having finite local-field descent with the G-tensors and geometrically in the G-orbit of the original filtration under a tensor-preserving identification, B is over a finite extension K/K₀ inside C_w and a*Fil¹H¹_dR(B)=(F_A¹)^⊕n after common finite extension. In (2) choose a complex embedding extending Qbar; κ's realizations use canonical model tensors and polarization. In (1) they equal its usual absolute-Hodge realizations.

claims.label: lem:auxiliary-datum
claims.statement: Given a Hodge embedding (G,X)→(GSp(V,ψ),Siegel) with G connected and multiplier c, for every prime p there exist a totally real P, connected reductive J and Hodge embedding (J,X_J)→GSp(W,ψ_W) such that: (i) G→J→Res_{P/Q}G_P are Shimura-data inclusions, first diagonal, and J imposes equal similitude multipliers; (ii) J_Qp is quasi-split and has a full connected stabilizer J_model making the triple strongly admissible; (iii) W≅(V⊗_Q P)^⊕m as rational J-representation for some m>0, ψ_W has common multiplier c, and J_model→GL(W_Qp) extends to a closed immersion into GL(Λ_p) for a self-dual Z_p lattice.

claims.label: lem:admissible-realization
claims.statement: Let (J,X_J,J_model) be strongly admissible with J_Qp quasi-split, using the adapted embedding and neat level, and let x∈S_K(F) have a characteristic-zero lift. Suppose a filtration F on D_x over finite extension of K₀ is admissible and geometrically induced by a J-valued cocharacter in the X_J conjugacy class. After a further finite extension there exist y∈I_x, a single tensor-preserving quasi-isogeny b:C_x→C_y and a lift y~ over the extended valuation ring such that b*Fil¹H¹_dR(C_y~)=F¹. Admissibility follows in particular from weak admissibility plus finite local-field descent of the filtered isocrystal and tensor data.

claims.label: cor:cm-transport
claims.statement: For every positive-dimensional A/Qbar with good reduction at w and rational Hodge γ∈H^{2r}(A(C),Q(r)), 0≤r≤dim A, there are n>0, a CM abelian B/Qbar with good reduction, a rational Hodge κ of codimension r and one quasi-isogeny a:A₀^n→B₀ with γ₀=(aj)*κ₀, j first-factor inclusion. This is one equality of usual absolute-Hodge specializations in every prime-to-p realization and crystalline cohomology extended to C_w.

claims.label: thm:filtration
claims.statement: Let A₀/F have a rational CM-field E action and a polarization whose Rosati induces conjugation on E. Suppose D=H¹_cris(A₀/W(F))[1/p] has rank 2s over E⊗K₀ with s≥1, and some invertible u∈End⁰(A₀) satisfies u†=u and ue=bar e u for all e∈E. Let β be the dual polarization into the slope-one isocrystal line. Then there are finite K/K₀ and L⊂D_K whose degree-(0,1) filtration is weakly admissible, with L E- and u-stable and β-Lagrangian, dim_Ω L_τ=s for every E-embedding over every algebraically closed Ω/K, and finite local-field descent of the indicated filtered tensor data. Geometrically all balanced E-stable β-Lagrangians form one orbit under G_D={g∈GSp(D,β)∩GL_{E⊗K₀}(D):det_{E⊗K₀}g=c(g)^s}; each is the weight-one subspace of a weights-(0,1) cocharacter of G_D. In particular L belongs to any original balanced polarized filtration orbit under tensor-preserving comparison.

claims.label: lem:avoidance
claims.statement: For every finite K₁/K₀ and integers r,b≥1, there exist θ algebraic over Q_p and (x₀,…,x_{r−1})∈K₁(θ)^r such that every nonzero polynomial in K₁[X₀,…,X_{r−1}] of total degree at most b is nonzero at that point. All x_i may be chosen in Q_p(θ). The coefficient field is the fixed K₁, not K₁(θ).

claims.label: lem:lagrangian-intersection
claims.statement: Let M be a 2m-dimensional symplectic space over characteristic-zero k, and W⊂M have dimension a. A nonempty open subset of its Lagrangian Grassmannian consists of L with dim(L∩W)=max(0,a−m). On any fixed symplectic affine big cell, some nonzero polynomial of degree at most m has nonvanishing locus contained in that open; this degree bound is independent of W.

claims.label: cor:filtration-admissible
claims.statement: The filtration constructed in thm:filtration, with its finite local-field descent, is admissible: its descended filtered isocrystal is the filtered crystalline module of a crystalline representation.

claims.label: cor:filtration-divisor
claims.statement: For D,L from thm:filtration, let ψ and U be the homological polarization and u-action on D_K∨. The untwisted divisor form ψ(−,U−) belongs to Fil¹(Λ²D_K)=L∧D_K and hence to filtration degree zero after the codimension-one Tate twist. If a marked power is realized by an abelian lift, the corresponding pulled-back divisor satisfies lem:lift-hom's filtration condition for its symmetric homomorphism.

claims.label: prop:weil
claims.statement: For every γ∈W_E^s(A) in the balanced good-reduction setting, γ₀ has the Lefschetz pairing property at w. More precisely, if U={u∈End⁰(A₀):u†=u, ue=bar e u for all e∈E} has no invertible element, all complementary pairings vanish. If U has an invertible element, γ₀ is one simultaneous rational Lefschetz class, not merely locally divisor-generated in separate realizations.

claims.label: lem:weil-orthogonality
claims.statement: If the rational anti-linear Rosati-symmetric space U has no invertible element, every specialization of every class in W_E^s(A) pairs to zero with every complementary Lefschetz class, in each realization.

claims.label: lem:weil-divisor-span
claims.statement: Let B be complex abelian, R∈End⁰(B) an idempotent and E→R End⁰(B)R an algebra action with unit R. Let T=im(R) on rational first homology have E-dimension 2s, with those endomorphisms zero on ker R. Suppose a rational divisor D has R*D=D and, over a splitting field, D=Σ_τD_τ with D_τ∈Λ²T_τ∨⊗Q(1) nondegenerate, with no cross-embedding terms. Then the rational subspace whose extension is ⊕_τΛ^{2s}T_τ∨⊗Q(s), extended by zero on the complementary summand, consists of rational Lefschetz classes on B.

claims.label: lem:weil-group
claims.statement: The Hodge homomorphism of balanced A factors through G={a∈GSp(V,ψ)∩GL_E(V):det_E a=c(a)^s}, and its conjugacy class defines a Hodge-type Shimura datum via that embedding. Over an algebraically closed field the corresponding filtration orbit on H¹ consists exactly of E-stable Lagrangians for the dual polarization having dimension s at every embedding. With a Tate-line basis, every determinant form in eq:weil-pure-space transforms by c^s.

claims.label: lem:cm-reduction
claims.statement: For every CM abelian A/Qbar with good reduction at w, r>0 and rational Hodge γ∈H^{2r}(A(C),Q(r)), there are finitely many good-reduction B_i/Qbar, rational homomorphisms f_i:A→B_i and rational Weil classes η_i∈H^{2r}(B_i(C),Q(r)) with γ=Σf_i*η_i. Each B_i has a CM-field K action with H₁ of K-rank 2r, Hodge signatures (r,r) at every embedding and a polarization inducing conjugation on K. The equality specializes with the same rational coefficients in every realization in thm:main. The proof constructs these via rational-idempotent factors of actual powers of A; it uses only balanced signatures, not split Weil type.

claims.label: cor:cm-pairing
claims.statement: The specialization of every rational Hodge class on a CM abelian variety over Qbar with good reduction at w has the Lefschetz pairing property.

claims.label: cor:all-hodge-specialization
claims.statement: With p,w and one good rational Tate-class theory R fixed before varying A, for every good-reduction abelian A/Qbar of dimension d, 0≤r≤d and rational Hodge γ∈H^{2r}(A(C),Q(r)), there exists a unique ρ_γ∈R^r(A₀) satisfying (ρ_γ)_ℓ=γ_{0,ℓ} for all ℓ≠p and (ρ_γ)_p⊗1=γ_{0,p} over C_w. This holds for every p, including 2. Uniqueness is in that fixed cohomological theory, not in the Chow group.

claims.label: cor:algebraic-specialization
claims.statement: Using the additional CM Hodge theorem OpenAICMHodge2026, Theorem 1.1, for every good-reduction A/Qbar of dimension d and rational Hodge γ∈H^{2r}(A(C),Q(r)), 0≤r≤d, there is one z_γ∈CH^r(A₀)_Q whose ℓ-adic classes equal γ_{0,ℓ} for all ℓ≠p and whose crystalline class extended to C_w equals γ_{0,p}. This holds for all p including 2. For every y∈CH^{d−r}(A₀)_Q, all corresponding trace pairings equal deg(z_γ·y)∈Q. The representing Chow class is not claimed unique, no lift of it to A is claimed, and no arbitrary characteristic-zero abelian HC is concluded.

claims.label: build/sections/00_intro.tex:L3-L15
claims.statement: Milne's pairing rationality asks that after good reduction a rational Hodge class have rational complementary divisor-product pairings, with one rational value in all realizations even for new nonlifting divisors. The manuscript states its precise claimed solution in thm:main; its cited antecedent pairing formulation is Milne2009 Conjecture 4.1 and MilneAIM2007 Section 10.

claims.label: build/sections/00_intro.tex:L66-L71
claims.statement: As described here, weak rationality asks that a specialized CM Hodge class whose components lie in the local spans of divisor products in every realization arise from one rational Lefschetz class. Only this manuscript's description is inventoried; the external full conjecture has not been read.

claims.label: build/sections/00_intro.tex:L149-L157
claims.statement: The source describes Milne's question whether a specialized CM Hodge class and a divisor lift together, up to isogeny, to a CM variety, and a conditional rationality criterion through weak lifting of Lefschetz classes on CM Weil triples. These are historical antecedents, not assumptions substituted for this manuscript's local prescribed-filtration construction; the source does not reproduce the full external statements.

claims.label: build/sections/02_transport.tex:L64-L79
claims.statement: Transport alternative (2) requires a degree-(0,1) weakly admissible filtration on D_A over a finite extension of K₀, finite local-field descent together with the specialized G-structure tensors, and membership after geometric tensor-preserving identification in the G-orbit of the original Hodge filtration. Weak admissibility alone without these other hypotheses is not the stated input.

claims.label: build/sections/03_filtration.tex:L40-L52
claims.statement: The filtration theorem requires an invertible rational endomorphism u of the reduced abelian variety, Rosati self-adjoint and conjugate-linear over the given CM field: ue=bar e u for all e. The main argument does not assume such a u always exists: prop:weil treats its nonexistence by a zero-pairing branch.

claims.label: build/sections/05_reduction.tex:L370-L373
claims.statement: The source invokes OpenAI's 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties', Theorem 1.1, to represent every rational Hodge class on the complex CM auxiliary B by a rational algebraic cycle. This is an additional input solely to cor:algebraic-specialization, not to the rationality theorem or CM transport. That October 6 manuscript was not among the assigned sources and was not read.

claims.label: build/sections/00_intro.tex:L116-L123
claims.statement: Every Hodge class on an abelian variety is absolute Hodge; its p-adic realization has the comparison compatibility invoked in lem:comparison, including the perfect-residue-field version for local auxiliary lifts. This supplies compatible realizations, not rational intersections with new divisors by itself.

claims.label: build/sections/01_preliminaries.tex:L86-L106
claims.statement: For an abelian X/F, Lef^r(X) realizes injectively and its scalar extension is the divisor-generated subspace in every relevant cohomology, including crystalline. Intersection gives a perfect rational pairing with Lef^{dim X−r}; homomorphism pushforward preserves local divisor-generated subspaces; hard Lefschetz and its inverse restrict to them. Extension from crystalline coefficients to C_w preserves these statements.

claims.statement: After one integer clears both the Tate-lattice and prescribed f₀ denominators, Tate's extension theorem extends the resulting integral generic-fiber p-divisible-group map over R. Faithfulness of the special-fiber Dieudonné functor and torsion-freeness identify its reduction with Nf₀.

claims.statement: Specified-map Serre–Tate deformation theory supplies compatible lifts over R/m^n of an algebraic special-fiber homomorphism together with the matching p-divisible-group lift. Formal existence algebraizes the resulting map when its source is proper over the complete noetherian R and target separated of finite type. The source's shear argument connects the fixed-object formulation to specified maps.

claims.label: build/sections/02_transport.tex:L229-L249
claims.statement: For the constructed strongly admissible Hodge datum, the source applies the adapted symplectic embedding theorem to obtain a self-dual Z_p lattice and integral closed immersion. It asserts the rational representation built in that theorem stays a sum of copies of U=V⊗P and that p=2 is included using the reduced-relative-root condition. The copy-preservation assertion is explicitly read off from the cited proof in the manuscript, not externally checked here.

claims.label: build/sections/02_transport.tex:L251-L301
claims.statement: At neat prime-to-p level and the adapted parahoric level, the source invokes the Hodge-type integral model, universal abelian scheme, defining tensors and compatible Betti/étale/crystalline frame torsors. It then extends any added rational J-invariant tensor by evaluating it in those torsors and argues comparison and a single tensor-preserving quasi-isogeny preserve all such tensors simultaneously. Only the canonical sections/torsors are the imported input; the extension-to-added-tensors argument is in this manuscript.

claims.label: build/sections/02_transport.tex:L304-L308
claims.statement: The special-point theorem is invoked to choose y in the tensor isogeny class I_x with a special-point (hence CM) lift and one quasi-isogeny from C_x preserving crystalline and all prime-to-p tensors. The later proof takes the CM lift over Qbar with the specified reduction place via canonical-model theory.

claims.label: build/sections/02_transport.tex:L404-L442
claims.statement: For the faithful local Hodge representation, the admissible-locus identity is invoked with ρ^−1(Z_GL)⊂Z_J. The crystalline period map from the framed local Shimura variety has image the J-admissible locus and is étale, so its nonempty fiber over the prescribed classical flag yields a point over a finite extension. The source separately identifies the cohomological period convention, including dual Frobenius descent and the marking.

claims.label: build/sections/02_transport.tex:L474-L480
claims.statement: The integral-uniformization hypothesis (U_x) is asserted to hold for the adapted global Hodge-type datum by Gleason–Lim–Xu Corollary 6.3, with Pappas–Rapoport Remark 4.10.4 also cited. This is a cited prerequisite of Theorem 4.10.6, not a condition proved by the inventory.

claims.label: build/sections/02_transport.tex:L461-L494
claims.statement: For global Hodge type, a full connected Bruhat–Tits stabilizer, an adapted integral Hodge embedding, the center's split-rank condition and (U_x), the source invokes a normal formal integral local Shimura variety with a map Θ_x to the completed global model. It is the tensor-compatible open-and-closed part of the Siegel Rapoport–Zink pullback, identifies the tautological framed shtuka and universal p-divisible group, and has the stated local Shimura variety as rigid generic fiber. The source claims the needed theorems include p=2.

claims.label: build/sections/02_transport.tex:L506-L566
claims.statement: The source invokes comparison of the constructed framed point's Breuil–Kisin and Dieudonné specializations and the special-fiber uniformization/isogeny-class map. With identity prime-to-p coordinate, it gives y=i_x(g) and a single abelian quasi-isogeny b:C_x→C_y preserving every designated realization, with the same crystalline marking used by the period map; thus the prescribed flag is b*Fil¹. The displayed cohomological Frobenius is ρ∨(σ(b_x))σ and the lattice is ρ∨(σ(g))D_x_integral.

claims.label: build/sections/02_transport.tex:L569-L574
claims.statement: For filtered isocrystal data descended to a finite local field, weak admissibility implies admissibility by Colmez–Fontaine. In the applications N=0 gives a crystalline representation, and scalar extension supplies admissibility over the finite extension of K₀. The source expressly restricts inequalities to descended subobjects before applying the theorem.

claims.label: build/sections/05_reduction.tex:L11-L16
claims.statement: The source attributes the stronger reduction of CM Hodge classes to pullbacks of classes on split-Weil-type varieties to Deligne and André, with Milne's reconstruction cited. Its own lem:cm-reduction instead proves the weaker balanced-signature version directly and does not assume split Hermitian type.

claims.label: build/sections/00_intro.tex:L142-L147
claims.statement: For an imaginary quadratic field, the introduction cites algebraicity of Weil classes on abelian fourfolds of Weil type and abelian sixfolds of split Weil type. It explicitly treats these as characteristic-zero antecedents, not as the arbitrary-dimensional input for its rationality proof.

claims.label: build/sections/00_intro.tex:L80-L96
claims.statement: Rationality for all CM abelian varieties is cited as equivalent to existence of a good theory of rational Tate classes on F-varieties with components products of abelian varieties and projective spaces. Such a theory chooses rational graded algebras whose scalar extensions are the Tate algebras, stable under pullback/pushforward, containing divisors and CM Hodge specializations; it does not assert these classes algebraic.

claims.label: build/sections/00_intro.tex:L74-L77
claims.statement: A CM abelian variety with simple ordinary reduction, and all its powers, is cited as a previous positive rationality case because every divisor on the reduction lifts.

dependency_map.statement: Under Hg(V)=SO(V,q), the asserted equivalence converts an actual nonzero algebraic V→H²(B) map, equivalently a cover with nonzero traced wedge, into every prescribed full KS tensor. It does not construct the initial input.

Very-general input in a polarized component, exact flat-cycle specialization, restriction to the actual transcendental summand and change of standard data give the claimed componentwise result; the all-projective-K3 corollary additionally requires the input in the needed components in every degree.

The abelian double-cover construction produces a fixed rank-eight quadratic variation, coherent Gauss half-sums and curve-product domination. The K3 realization uses its Y cup form; the map to the X eigenspace scales that form by two.

Integral enlargement and root monodromy feed period-stack contraction/descent on the original parameter line, supplying the K3 pencil and its claimed uniruled quadratic pullbacks without replacing the base by an arbitrary cover.

The two-square construction converts a specified VHS comparison into a surface correspondence at points outside a countable exceptional set. Fixed models and degree-three cycles precede the varying b; the proof's difference cylinders have self-composition −4 on the relevant summand.
A nonzero algebraic map to a curve-product is upgraded, using both full half-spin orientations and algebraic weight-one slot maps, to the specified rank-eight full even-Clifford tensor.

Whole-rank-eight Hilbert specialization includes Picard jumps, then compression and rational period/isometry transfer give the actual prescribed tensor on T_S for every rational isometric embedding into V_P. Buskin is an imported rational-Hodge-isometry input; rank or signature alone is not the locus condition.

One exact algebraic full-Clifford tensor is the independent criterion for HC/GHC on all K3 self-powers. Applying it on the quadratic locus and then the cited motivic decompositions gives the stated Hilbert-scheme/moduli consequences. The general criterion is not restricted to rank eight.

As a logical composition of unverified assertions, choose cup-form full-Clifford data in ks10's conditional conclusion and feed that exact tensor to ks30's general criterion to obtain conditional HC/GHC in the component. The September 30 paper does not cite the September 10 paper or declare this as its proof dependency; its rank-eight geometric route is separate.

The introduction cites Weil-fourfold/OG6 and quaternionic-class literature as context distinguishing an algebraic embedding from the exact KS map. It does not cite the excluded standalone Weil manuscript as an input to its main theorem.

One actual tensor-preserving special-fiber quasi-isogeny and rational polarization normalization transport the class in all realizations. CM transport and prescribed-filtration transport are different alternatives; the latter's local lift need not be CM and no generic-fiber isogeny is claimed.

In the invertible Rosati anti-linear branch, bounded-degree avoidance and symplectic intersection bounds produce the constrained weakly admissible filtration with finite local-field descent. The cited finite-local-field theorem then supplies admissibility; u-stability supplies the divisor filtration condition.

The assigned internal Weil section proves the claimed pairing dichotomy: no invertible u gives zero pairings; invertible u permits a local lift on which a suitable divisor generates the pure determinant space, giving one rational Lefschetz specialization. General characteristic-zero algebraicity of all Weil classes is not an input.

The manuscript's direct balanced-Weil decomposition of CM Hodge classes and functorial pairing property give CM rationality. The stronger imported split-Weil antecedent is contextual; balanced signatures suffice for the stated argument.

Transport an arbitrary abelian Hodge class to a CM auxiliary on special fibers, apply CM rationality, and pull back complementary Lefschetz pairings. This is the main all-prime rationality route and does not invoke OpenAICMHodge2026.

CM rationality supplies a good rational Tate-class theory via Milne2009 Theorem 4.5; fix it once. CM transport and its pullback/injectivity axioms give unique membership of every Hodge specialization in that cohomological theory, not algebraicity.

The separately cited October 6 CM Hodge theorem makes the CM auxiliary class algebraic; spreading to Qbar, good-reduction specialization and rational pullback give one cycle for all stated realizations. This additional conclusion is distinct from thm:main and from membership in a fixed good theory.

The standalone Weil manuscript was excluded and not read. No direct dependency from it to either KS theorem or the main Milne rationality theorem is established by these assigned sources. Milne's own build/sections/04_weil.tex was assigned and read. Milne does not cite either assigned KS paper; its external CM-Hodge input cannot be expanded into an unseen Weil dependency here.

unverified_possible_gaps.statement: The initial actual cycle or trace-nonzero cover is an explicit assumption, not a result of the reduction. Any later use claiming unconditional KS algebraicity must separately supply it in the required components. This is a scope warning, not a defect found in the conditional theorem.

A later audit should track oriented period planes, signed square roots, connected spin lifts, full parity multiplicities, duality and slot ordering through changes of rational quadratic polarization. Exact prescribed-map recovery is stronger than recovering some nonzero Hodge embedding; no orientation error is established here.

The source arguments require the whole flat rational cycle class, not only its generic transcendental action, to specialize through proper Hilbert parameters, including singular/nonreduced parameter spaces and Picard-jump algebraic directions. The hypotheses and coefficient preservation remain unaudited mathematically.

High-value checks include signs of j and δ, the factor-two relation between Y and X cup forms, integral lattice enlargement, local root monodromy and descent on the original line. The manuscript distinguishes these forms and lattices; their asserted compatibility is not certified here.

The two-square comparison depends on the signed cylinder self-composition −4, a canonical Leray/localization comparison and removal of boundary maps using fixed Hodge structures. The compactifications and degree-three correspondence must be fixed before b varies; this quantifier order deserves a later audit, not an asserted gap.

Surjectivity for the full rational Hodge-Hom space, descent from both complex half-spin orientations, minus the geometric tensor flip, and exact compression to T_S are critical. Neither a simple spin factor nor a generic nonzero vector map alone would state the claimed conclusion. No failed identity is asserted.

The all-prime claim, especially p=2, needs the exact cited strongly admissible/adapted-embedding hypotheses, center condition, (U_x), period admissibility and matching marked quasi-isogeny conventions. External papers were not opened, so their applicability and precise version-dependent locators are unverified.

The source's identification of all local polarization similitudes with one rational intersection-number ratio, and κ=λ^(−r)η_B/[P:Q], is central to simultaneous rather than separate local transport. Compatibility for local auxiliary Betti structures and specified rational algebraic homomorphisms is a distinct check; arbitrary Q_p-linear maps are not the stated lifting input.

Avoidance only controls bounded-degree polynomials over the fixed coefficient field before adjoining θ. The subsequent weak-admissibility inequalities for all K₀-subisocrystals, descent of all tensors to a finite local field and preservation of the balanced group orbit remain separate unverified steps.

The proof needs rational descent of the full Galois-stable determinant sum, not rationality of individual embedding lines, and compatible rational projectors/pullbacks on actual abelian factors. The noninvertible and invertible branches must not be conflated with a general characteristic-zero Weil algebraicity theorem.

The stronger algebraic-specialization conclusion explicitly depends on the unread October 6 CM-Hodge Theorem 1.1. No validity assessment of that theorem, or of any possible dependency it has on an excluded Weil manuscript, is made. Main rationality is source-declared independent of this extra input.

source_parsing_notes.statement: All 20 staged .tex files in exactly the three listed source_path_base directories were read, including all 17 input/include targets, the September 10 dependency table, the Milne figure and every bibliography. source_path is family-relative inside a manuscript record, coverage paths are campaign-relative, and all spans are inclusive 1-based lines. A prose claim's label is its unique primary source-line locator; additional_source_locators identify disjoint supporting passages rather than pretending they form one environment.

Namespace prefixes distinguish colliding labels such as main:theorem. The references arrays intentionally include equation and section labels as well as claim IDs; these resolve against the assigned source labels. A dependency reference can point to an introductory statement repeated later as a proof target and does not itself impose a new proof order.

established_import_as_cited records how the manuscript treats a cited result. Every claim, including imports and assumptions, remains asserted_unverified. Local JSON/span/link checks are inventory validation only, not a citation check against external sources or mathematical certification.

The three papers do not share one global notation: ks10 V has rank 21; ks30 V can mean T(1) or its rank-16 anti-invariant lattice, U is often rank eight, and M is either a theta bundle or a lattice. Milne uses both homological and cohomological group actions. In its CM reduction, A⊗_Q K denotes an actual power with an index-field action in the isogeny category, whereas V_K denotes scalar extension of a vector space.
